To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a new multi-task learning method, called Conflict-Averse Gradient Desent (CAGD), which is guaranteed to converge to Pareto-stationarity.
we propose a new multi-task optimization algorithm, which has the same computational complexity as standard gradient descent, but converges to the Pareto-optimal point of a multi-task loss function.

(a) we propose a new multi-task learning objective that can be optimized by a simple gradient descent algorithm and converges to a Pareto-optimal solution with convergence rate O(1/T); (b) we propose a conflict-averse gradient descent method that can converge to Pareto-stationarity in O(1/T) rate, which can be used to optimize any multi-task learning objective.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce the concept of Conflict-Averse Gradient Descents (CAGD) for optimizing multi-task objectives, and propose a general framework for CAGD.
we provide a novel theoretical analysis for the multi-task learning problem and propose a simple yet efficient algorithm for solving this problem.
we propose a novel algorithm for multi-task learning that provably converges to a Pareto-optimal solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the average objective, the Pareto-stationarity is not the right concept to measure convergence.
we provide a principled way to manipulate task gradients to avoid conflicting gradients.
we provide the first convergence guarantee for a class of multi-task learning algorithms, and the guarantee holds for the entire Pareto set of the objective, which is the best possible result.
